page: UpCloud GPU-12xCPU-128GB-2xL4 is a GPU-accelerated server instance configured with 12 vCPUs and 128.0 GB of system memory. The processing power is delivered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor built on the x86_64 architecture, featuring 12 physical cores with a single thread per core under a shared CPU allocation model. The instance includes two NVIDIA L4 GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, providing a combined total of 48 GB of VRAM. There is no local storage bundled with this server type, and virtualization is managed via the KVM hypervisor.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all placing in the top tier. Conversely, multi-core operations, including stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, fall into the average tier. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks, along with PassMark CPU and memory scores, also align with average tier performance. For language model workloads, the server achieves top-tier text generation speeds of 349.81 tokens per second using a small 135M model, while prompt processing for the same model remains in the average tier.

The qualitative cost efficiency of this instance is defined by its high GPU-to-vCPU density, pairing 48 GB of VRAM with 128.0 GB of system memory. This resource distribution makes the instance suitable for workloads that require dedicated graphics acceleration but do not demand massive multi-core CPU scaling, such as small-scale LLM inference, machine learning model training, and data science tasks. A notable tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation and the absence of local storage, which requires external storage attachments for data-intensive applications.

The hardware configuration includes two NVIDIA L4 Ada Lovelace GPUs delivering 48 GB of total VRAM, while local storage is absent. Operating under a KVM hypervisor with shared CPU allocation, the server exhibits top-tier single-core CPU performance, single-threaded compression, and small-model LLM text generation. However, multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations remain in the average tier. This resource profile offers high GPU and memory density relative to its vCPU count, making it suitable for machine learning inference, data science, and GPU-accelerated workloads that do not require dedicated local storage or high multi-threaded CPU scaling.
